events.title: The Greensboro lunch counter sit-in begins
events.summary: Four African Americans sit down at a segregated Woolworth's counter and refuse to leave.
events.description: On February 1, 1960, four African Americans began a sit-in at a segregated Woolworth's lunch counter in Greensboro, North Carolina, a protest that helped spark sit-ins across the American South.
events.notificationBody: In 1960, four African Americans sat in at a segregated Woolworth's counter in Greensboro.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 1

events.title: Puccini's La Boheme premieres in Turin
events.summary: Giacomo Puccini's opera opens at the Teatro Regio.
events.description: On February 1, 1896, Giacomo Puccini's opera La Boheme had its premiere at the Teatro Regio in Turin, Italy.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 1

events.title: Trygve Lie is elected the first UN secretary-general
events.summary: A Norwegian statesman becomes the United Nations' first chief.
events.description: On February 1, 1946, the Norwegian politician and diplomat Trygve Lie was elected the first secretary-general of the United Nations.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 1
Encyclopaedia Britannica - Trygve Lie

events.title: Space shuttle Columbia breaks up over Texas
events.summary: All seven astronauts are lost as the shuttle returns to Earth.
events.description: On February 1, 2003, the US space shuttle Columbia broke up at an altitude of about 40 miles (60 km) over Texas while returning to Earth, killing all seven crew members.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 1

events.title: Johanna Sigurdardottir becomes Iceland's first woman prime minister
events.summary: Iceland swears in its first female head of government.
events.description: On February 1, 2009, Johanna Sigurdardottir was sworn in as prime minister of Iceland, the first woman to hold the post.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 1

events.title: Punxsutawney turns to a groundhog for a forecast
events.summary: A Pennsylvania town begins its famous Groundhog Day tradition.
events.description: On February 2, 1887, a group in Punxsutawney, Pennsylvania, went looking for a groundhog to predict the weather, beginning the town's Groundhog Day tradition.
events.notificationBody: In 1887, a group in Punxsutawney, Pennsylvania, sought a groundhog to predict the weather.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 2

events.title: The Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo is signed
events.summary: The treaty ends the Mexican-American War.
events.description: On February 2, 1848, the United States and Mexico signed the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo, ending the Mexican-American War.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 2

events.title: F.W. de Klerk lifts the ban on the African National Congress
events.summary: South Africa's president opens the way to Mandela's release.
events.description: On February 2, 1990, South African President F.W. de Klerk lifted the 30-year ban on the African National Congress, leading to Nelson Mandela's release from prison and marking the beginning of the end of apartheid.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 2

events.title: The Battle of Stalingrad ends
events.summary: The last German troops in the city surrender to the Soviets.
events.description: On February 2, 1943, the Battle of Stalingrad ended with the surrender of German troops to the Soviet army, a turning point of World War II.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 2
Encyclopaedia Britannica - Battle of Stalingrad

events.title: James Joyce is born in Dublin
events.summary: The author of Ulysses is born.
events.description: On February 2, 1882, the Irish writer James Joyce, author of Ulysses, was born in Dublin.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - James Joyce
Encyclopaedia Britannica - Ulysses

events.title: Eileen Collins becomes the first woman to pilot a space shuttle
events.summary: She takes the pilot's seat aboard Discovery.
events.description: On February 3, 1995, the American astronaut Eileen Collins became the first woman to pilot a space shuttle, flying aboard Discovery.
events.notificationTitle: A first in the shuttle's front seat
events.notificationBody: In 1995, Eileen Collins became the first woman to pilot a space shuttle.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 3

events.title: The Fifteenth Amendment is ratified
events.summary: The US Constitution bars denying the vote on the basis of race.
events.description: On February 3, 1870, the Fifteenth Amendment to the US Constitution was ratified, guaranteeing Americans the right to vote regardless of race.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 3

events.title: Felix Mendelssohn is born
events.summary: The German composer who bridged Classical and Romantic music is born.
events.description: On February 3, 1809, the German composer Felix Mendelssohn was born. He largely followed Classical models while helping to shape Romanticism.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 3

events.title: Umm Kulthum dies in Cairo
events.summary: One of the most famous Arab singers of the 20th century dies.
events.description: On February 3, 1975, the Egyptian singer Umm Kulthum, one of the most famous Arab singers and public figures of the 20th century, died in Cairo.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 3

events.title: Buddy Holly is killed in a plane crash
events.summary: The rock 'n' roll singer dies at age 22.
events.description: On February 3, 1959, the American rock 'n' roll singer Buddy Holly was killed in a plane crash at age 22.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 3

events.title: TheFacebook.com is launched at Harvard
events.summary: Four Harvard students launch the social network that becomes Facebook.
events.description: On February 4, 2004, Harvard students Mark Zuckerberg, Eduardo Saverin, Dustin Moskovitz and Chris Hughes founded and launched the website TheFacebook.com, which became Facebook.
events.notificationTitle: The dorm-room site that went global
events.notificationBody: In 2004, Harvard students launched TheFacebook.com, the site that became Facebook.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 4

events.title: Ceylon gains independence from Britain
events.summary: The island now called Sri Lanka ends more than 150 years of British control.
events.description: On February 4, 1948, Ceylon, now Sri Lanka, gained independence from Great Britain, which had controlled the island since 1796.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 4

events.title: The Yalta Conference opens
events.summary: Roosevelt, Churchill and Stalin meet as World War II nears its end.
events.description: On February 4, 1945, in the final stages of World War II, the Yalta Conference opened with Franklin D. Roosevelt, Winston Churchill and Joseph Stalin.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 4

events.title: George Washington is elected the first US president
events.summary: The first electoral college votes for him unanimously.
events.description: On February 4, 1789, George Washington was elected the first president of the United States by a unanimous vote of the first electoral college.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 4

events.title: Lake Placid hosts the first Winter Olympics in the United States
events.summary: The Winter Games come to New York state.
events.description: On February 4, 1932, the United States hosted its first Winter Olympic Games, in Lake Placid, New York.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 4

events.title: Mexico adopts its present constitution
events.summary: The constitution that still governs Mexico is adopted.
events.description: On February 5, 1917, Mexico adopted its present constitution, which holds that the government should take an active role in the country's day-to-day affairs.
events.notificationBody: In 1917, Mexico adopted the constitution that still governs the country today.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 5

events.title: The first Hay-Pauncefote Treaty is signed
events.summary: The United States and Britain negotiate over a future canal across Panama.
events.description: On February 5, 1900, the United States and Great Britain signed the first of two Hay-Pauncefote treaties over control of the proposed Panama Canal.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 5

events.title: Apollo 14 lands on the Moon
events.summary: Alan Shepard and Edgar Mitchell touch down in the Fra Mauro highlands.
events.description: On February 5, 1971, Apollo 14's lunar module landed in the Fra Mauro highlands of the Moon. Commander Alan Shepard later swung at two golf balls with a makeshift club.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - Apollo 14
NASA - Apollo 14

events.title: Cristiano Ronaldo is born in Funchal
events.summary: The Portuguese soccer star is born.
events.description: On February 5, 1985, the soccer player Cristiano Ronaldo was born in Funchal, Portugal.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 5

events.title: Colin Powell presents the case against Iraq at the UN
events.summary: The US secretary of state argues that Iraq holds weapons of mass destruction.
events.description: On February 5, 2003, US Secretary of State Colin Powell appeared before the United Nations Security Council to present evidence that Iraq possessed weapons of mass destruction.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 5

events.title: The Treaty of Waitangi is signed
events.summary: The British Crown and Maori chiefs sign New Zealand's founding document.
events.description: On February 6, 1840, the British and Maori chiefs of the North Island signed the Treaty of Waitangi (Te Tiriti o Waitangi).
events.notificationTitle: The treaty at the heart of New Zealand
events.notificationBody: In 1840, the British Crown and Maori chiefs signed the Treaty of Waitangi.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 6

events.title: Elizabeth II becomes queen
events.summary: She succeeds her father, King George VI.
events.description: On February 6, 1952, Elizabeth II ascended the throne of the United Kingdom following the death of her father, King George VI.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 6

events.title: Bob Marley is born
events.summary: The Jamaican singer-songwriter who took reggae worldwide is born.
events.description: On February 6, 1945, the singer-songwriter Bob Marley was born. He found stardom blending ska, rock steady and reggae.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 6

events.title: Babe Ruth is born
events.summary: The home-run hitter becomes one of America's most celebrated athletes.
events.description: On February 6, 1895, the baseball player Babe Ruth was born. His home-run hitting made him one of the most celebrated athletes in American sports.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 6

events.title: SpaceX's Falcon Heavy makes its first test flight
events.summary: A new heavy-lift rocket launches for the first time.
events.description: On February 6, 2018, SpaceX's Falcon Heavy launch vehicle made its first test flight.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 6

events.title: The Beatles land in New York City
events.summary: Beatlemania crosses the Atlantic.
events.description: On February 7, 1964, the Beatles landed in New York City.
events.notificationBody: In 1964, the Beatles landed in New York City.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 7

events.title: Charlie Chaplin's Little Tramp debuts
events.summary: Chaplin's most famous character first appears on screen.
events.description: On February 7, 1914, Charlie Chaplin debuted his most famous screen character, the Little Tramp, in the film Kid Auto Races at Venice.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 7

events.title: Charles Dickens is born in Portsmouth
events.summary: The author of Oliver Twist and A Christmas Carol is born.
events.description: On February 7, 1812, the novelist Charles Dickens was born in Portsmouth, England.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 7
Encyclopaedia Britannica - Charles Dickens

events.title: Grenada gains independence from Britain
events.summary: The Caribbean island becomes an independent nation.
events.description: On February 7, 1974, Grenada gained independence from the United Kingdom.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 7

events.title: Abdullah II becomes king of Jordan
events.summary: He succeeds his father, King Hussein, hours after his death.
events.description: On February 7, 1999, Abdullah II became king of Jordan, hours after the death of his father, King Hussein.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 7
